scope: Primary sources consulted for the source-review addendum; separate from the original 18-source design catalog. Source findings are not native Windows execution evidence.

sources.title: Python os.replace and rename documentation
sources.supports: Successful rename atomicity is described as a POSIX requirement; same-filesystem replacement does not by itself establish power-loss durability.

sources.title: Python os.DirEntry.stat Windows identity fields
sources.supports: On Windows, DirEntry.stat zeroes st_ino, st_dev and st_nlink; use full stat where these values are required.

sources.title: Python pathlib general properties
sources.supports: PureWindowsPath comparison uses case folding; syntactic equality is insufficient to distinguish case-only siblings in an actually case-sensitive Windows directory.

sources.title: Microsoft MoveFileExW
sources.supports: Windows move/replace flags, same-volume directory behavior, cross-volume copying and write-through flag semantics. This does not independently prove a universal atomic-visibility or power-loss guarantee for every Python os.replace deployment.

sources.title: Microsoft ReplaceFileW
sources.supports: Replacement requires the same volume, documents failure states, and does not support REPLACEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH. It must not be treated as a blanket durability guarantee.

sources.title: NIST SHA-256 worked examples
sources.supports: Official one- and two-block SHA-256 example message digests used by the retained independent probe.
